summary.intent: Build an AI agent product ('ask-soony') for the Lio hackathon challenge that continuously monitors Soony's supplier/launch data, finds contradictions and shortages, and acts on them (supplier emails, approvals, phone alerts), plus prepare the demo and hand-in by 12:00 Sunday.
summary.outcome: Analyzed the data and found the Collector's Edition shortfalls (art book overbooking, failed statues, sleeve revisions), then built a polling/versioned-store agent with a Today/Launch web UI, sign-off approval flow, demo instance, README, demo script and a phone-call bridge. The real Twilio test call was still being debugged at transcript end; the demo was restarted with calls off.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks; the documented approach is polling the file list and comparing SHA-256 checksums, since files are replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored `data/` folder and `.env` is gitignored; `.env.example` is committed. Nothing from the data should go into code or the repo.
Team workflow files `CLAUDE.md` and `PROGRESS.md` exist in the repo and tasks are claimed in `PROGRESS.md`.

Live and demo instances are separate servers (:8000 live, :8001 demo) behind a Cloudflare tunnel; `scripts/demo.sh` supports reset, snapshot, stop and restart, plus `CALLS=twilio` to enable real calls. Demo records supplier emails only in a dry outbox.
Live and demo servers share one alert database, so alert-to-case links are stored per state folder; `ASK_CARD_ALERTS=off` disables the phone bridge on live.
Phone calls default to `ASK_CALL_PROVIDER=dry_run`; real Twilio calls cost about $0.38 per minute and the keypad needs `ASK_PUBLIC_URL` set.
The web UI polls state every 5 s (`POLL_MS`) in `App.tsx`, so all pages update with a delay of up to 5 s; routine data refreshes every 15 s.
The shared mailbox sync used to write back an old copy of the action log and lose records recorded meanwhile; it now appends under the shared lock.
CSV exports in drops can have varied encodings and rows with more fields than the header; both the parser and the team's verifier needed robust readers.

code.finding: New bridge: every 30 s raises one phone alert for a red case or one due within 120 min untouched for 15 min, applies phone decisions exactly once to the case, closes alerts when the case is decided elsewhere.
AlertBook.decide now passes decisions on alerts linked to a case through to the case.
The login page has its own copy of the logo mark and the favicon link, which must be updated separately from the web app.

workflow: Check the Entire hook log to confirm sessions are tracked; it skips checkpoints when no repo files changed.
Parallelising builders (subagents) with writing docs worked well for the time-boxed hackathon; subagents did the 200-confirmation cross-check and the phone bridge.
Rehearsing the demo script end to end on the demo instance surfaced a real bug (a broken sentence on rev B cases).
Confirm with the user before costly or outward-facing actions such as real phone calls, supplier emails and DNS changes; pushes were done on the user's request.
Browser-driven checks (pressing J repeatedly and reading the highlighted row) verified the UI fix rather than assuming it.

friction: The Cloudflare demo hostname first pointed at the wrong tunnel, giving error 1033 until corrected.
The portal token was initially empty, which blocked the data fetch until the user added it.
Several edits to `scripts/demo.sh` did not apply because the line differed from what was expected, so restarts did not happen.
The real Twilio test call did not place on the first attempts and needed debugging of the bridge gating logic.
Safari caches favicons stubbornly, so the old yellow icon may keep showing.
The shared mailbox sync race lost the 07:58 art book approval record, which had to be restored from the Sent folder.
CSV encoding and header mismatches in new drops broke the data check and the verifier.
